Clinician: "it may be possible that you might be having an infection in the urine." Symptoms discussed include lower tummy pain, increased frequency, pink urine, feeling hot/sweaty, fitting suspected UTI based on these features.

Clinician: "Start taking them as soon as you get them."

Transcript documents only antibiotics and safety-net advice; there is no mention of ordering tests or recommending over-the-counter medications.
Follow-up/safety net: same quote as plan-004 – instructions to contact again if pain worsens, high temperature, back pain, new symptoms, or no improvement, with possible face-to-face exam.
Patient: "Like around 37." and clinician repeats "37."
Pain site: "So it's the lower tummy?" and question clarifying middle vs side, consistent with suprapubic/lower midline abdominal pain.
Patient: "there was some like slight blood in the urine, but like it was a little bit pink."
